authority: maintained status overlay on the generated acceptance-scenario register
evidencePolicy: PASS requires reproducible evidence; NOT_APPLICABLE requires a bounded profile rationale; UNKNOWN remains release-visible.

items.text: A new user opens Omnevum from a GitHub Pages deployment on a supported mobile browser, completes minimal/skippable onboarding, creates canonical records, closes/reopens, and retains data without a mandatory account or backend.
items.notes: Fresh local static Chromium, current-artifact in-app-browser, and exact-current-artifact Edge evidence cover the core no-account create/search/reload path plus two current-artifact domain owners; GitHub Pages, supported mobile rows, and full onboarding qualification remain open.

items.text: After the app shell is cached, the user performs core local workflows offline and sees explicit degradation only for capabilities that actually require network access.
items.notes: Fresh local static origins reloaded the cached shell offline, created canonical notes offline, and preserved them after network restoration; the historical receipt-bound Edge artifact repeated offline mutation/reload with a healthy derived index and empty app-origin diagnostics, while the historical Chromium artifact reported Failed to fetch for offline sync and kept local capture usable. GitHub Pages, Safari/Firefox, assistive technology, native fault behavior, and external provider qualification still require qualification.

items.text: The user changes branding from Omnevum to JohnOS, changes logo/theme/lens labels, upgrades Omnevum, and retains personal branding without changing canonical record identities.
items.notes: Built-artifact Chromium evidence covers JohnOS in-app branding, current-artifact French locale, custom labels/icons, theme, and reload persistence without semantic-count loss; logo/lens-label customization and upgrade/installed-host qualification remain open.

items.text: The user switches between accessible Light and AMOLED Dark themes; critical state, focus, text, charts, and interactions remain readable and accessible.
items.notes: Theme switching was observed in development smoke; current built Edge evidence records the labelled presentation control, 390x844 no-overflow metrics, visible labels, and a sequential keyboard path. WCAG conformance and all target rows remain unverified.

items.text: Safe Presentation Mode recovers from a deliberately broken custom presentation profile without deleting that profile or canonical data.
items.notes: Deterministic core/storage evidence and historical built Chromium interaction prove malformed presentation and canonical data are preserved while a known-good Safe Presentation profile is selected for the session; broader browser/accessibility/visual qualification and production deployment remain open.

items.text: The user switches UI locale, number/date formatting, and measurement presentation without altering canonical semantic values or translating user-authored content.
items.notes: French Canadian formatting/localization and reload persistence are covered locally; full measurement-presentation breadth, long-string/RTL/pseudolocalization, and target-matrix qualification remain open.

items.text: A canonical record appears in multiple authorized lenses/projections without creating unsynchronized writable copies.
items.notes: Compose and derived-data projections are exercised locally without a second writable owner; broader authorized-lens and permission-boundary qualification remains open.

items.text: Search index corruption is injected; Omnevum reports degradation, rebuilds the derived index, and canonical data remains intact.
items.notes: Deterministic fake-indexeddb injection is covered; native browser corruption and full target qualification remain open.

items.text: Storage quota pressure is injected; replaceable state is reclaimed before canonical data and the user receives explicit storage/backup guidance.
items.notes: Deterministic pressure injection reclaims derived search state and exposes Vault guidance; native browser quota exhaustion remains open.

items.text: A coherent Vault backup is exported on one major browser/platform family and restored on a materially different supported family with semantic IDs/revisions/provenance preserved.
items.notes: Integrity-protected Vault transfer preserves IDs/provenance across isolated local stores and bounded artifact restore; a real materially different browser-family/origin run and large-Vault qualification remain open.

items.text: The user syncs to at least one consumer cloud route and one zero-required-payment/self-hosted or owner-controlled route; provider migration preserves logical identity.
items.notes: The provider-neutral transport and owner-controlled localhost route are exercised against a bounded local replica, including pull/import/push identity preservation and truthful reporting when push fails after local import. Consumer-cloud qualification, provider migration, authentication, and zero-payment/self-host target qualification remain open.

items.text: A stale/offline replica reappears after deletion; tombstone/rejoin semantics prevent silent resurrection.
items.notes: Deterministic merge tests preserve tombstones and reject silent resurrection, and the built UI completes a local bounded pull/import/push. Offline replica interruption, browser rejoin, and a browser-level tombstone scenario remain open.

items.text: All product AI routes are disabled. Core data, Home, Search, visualization/modeling, backup/restore, and Recovery remain usable.
items.notes: The shipped profile keeps AI optional/inactive and the built core path remains usable; provider-removal and broader non-AI qualification are not complete.

items.text: The same shared AI broker is used by at least two distinct domain workflows without either domain owning provider credentials.
items.notes: One shared route registry/context broker serves distinct core.capture and core.track workflows while provider credentials remain outside domain owners. Shipped provider adapters and built-workflow qualification remain open.

items.text: An AI response containing malicious embedded instructions cannot expand context scope, switch provider/disclosure class, modify permissions, or execute a canonical mutation without the normal command/policy path.
items.notes: The broker fixes disclosure/source context, rejects unadmitted commands and authority-shaped arguments, bounds proposal sources, and requires the normal command path. Provider/process/browser adversarial qualification and command execution integration remain open.

items.text: One first-party module fails during startup/runtime; Home/System/Recovery and unrelated modules remain usable.
items.notes: The capability runtime isolates a failing optional module while core startup remains usable in deterministic tests and the current built preview. Native failure matrices and broader target qualification remain open.

items.text: An update/migration is intentionally interrupted. Omnevum does not silently reset data and offers a tested recovery/repair path.
items.notes: Local static Chromium service-worker update/rollback on the exact current artifact, malformed-state recovery snapshot, explicit repair-from-snapshot preserving valid records, deterministic stale-client fencing, an aborted IndexedDB upgrade followed by exact-record reopen, and exact-current-artifact Edge recovery-shell/read-only-export/repair interaction are covered; native quota/corruption behavior, browser-family breadth, accessibility, and production deployment remain open.

items.text: A user moves the static distribution from one HTTPS origin to another using Vault backup/sync rather than depending on browser-private origin storage migration.
items.notes: The user-mediated Vault path is proven across separate local stores and does not depend on browser-private origin migration; real HTTPS-origin handoff, UI file transfer, and deployment qualification remain open.

items.text: A fresh AI engineer creates a nontrivial stateful module using only the public Omnevum app contract and normal repository interfaces.
items.notes: The current browser receipt proves a nontrivial stateful declarative app can be created through the public factory contract and canonical command path; the two-process benchmark proves interrupted app resumption. Independent fresh-AI authorship, touch/mobile breadth, engine substitution, and human acceptance remain open.

items.text: A fresh AI engineer creates a nontrivial game using the same package/lifecycle infrastructure and proves save/resume, touch input, responsive behavior, and Recovery.
items.notes: The current browser receipt proves the public game contract, semantic controls, save/load, and desktop rendering; automated storage regressions and the two-process benchmark now prove package-state Vault export/import, Recovery repair retention, and interrupted resumption. Independent fresh-AI creation, touch hardware, mobile targets, engine substitution, native on-device Recovery interaction, and human acceptance remain open.

items.text: The engineering run is interrupted mid-project and a fresh agent resumes from repository/control state without the original conversation or repeated owner questions.
items.notes: The generated integrity-manifested Recovery bundle references the authority, control, evidence, source, tests, release, and restore procedure without secrets or absolute private paths. At exact detached revision f92fa4a, the clean-checkout benchmark reported FRESH_AGENT_NPM_CI_PASS, RECOVERY_AUDIT_PASS files=166, FRESH_AGENT_CI_PASS, FACTORY_INTERRUPTION_EXPECTED_STOP_PASS, FACTORY_INTERRUPTION_RESUME_PASS, FRESH_AGENT_FACTORY_INTERRUPTION_PASS, and clean-clone=true original-conversation=false after verifying canonical IDs/status plus package-state game seed/state. The worktree is removed after the complete CI and interruption/resume gates.

items.text: Upstream dependency change is detected, evaluated as a candidate, and either adopted, adapted, deferred, or rejected without silently breaking the released Omnevum contract.
items.notes: The current declared npm graph was checked with npm outdated and returned no candidate packages, with the exact lockfile, license, security, and control gates still passing. A future changed dependency candidate and isolated adopt/adapt/defer/reject contract run remain open.

items.text: The user substantially personalizes navigation, Home composition, terminology, typography/iconography, layout/density, branding, and theme without a source-code fork; the changes are reversible and do not alter canonical semantic IDs or permissions.
items.notes: Current and historical built previews prove bounded declarative branding, terminology, navigation visibility/order controls, Home composition, typeface, icon treatment, density, locale/theme contract, document metadata binding, standalone profile export/import, reload persistence, Recovery reachability, and unchanged canonical counts. Target accessibility/browser breadth, icon/logo assets, installed-host metadata, profile migration across future schemas, and release qualification remain open.

items.text: The user renames an installed system to JohnOS. All Omnevum-controlled in-app surfaces update immediately; on a target that does not dynamically update installed Home-Screen/OS metadata, Omnevum truthfully reports PLATFORM_LIMITED and provides the supported refresh/reinstall path without corrupting data/install identity.
items.notes: Local built-preview evidence covers controlled in-app rebranding, persistence, and the explicit PLATFORM_LIMITED report with a host refresh/re-add/reinstall path; actual installed-host refresh behavior, host breadth, and release qualification remain open.

items.text: The accepted core is deployed on the constrained GitHub Pages profile without custom server response headers/functions. Core security/privacy/durability claims that are made for that profile remain valid; a deliberately header-dependent optional feature is explicitly unavailable/degraded rather than silently assumed safe.
items.notes: A locked GitHub Pages build/upload/deploy workflow is configured with a relative-base artifact and static-host policy; no remote workflow run, live URL, clean-origin smoke, rollback, or target qualification is yet evidenced.

items.text: On a supported browser row where OPFS is unavailable or deliberately disabled, ordinary canonical structured records remain usable through the qualified fallback; only features that genuinely require unavailable large-file semantics degrade explicitly.
items.notes: IndexedDB remains the canonical structured-record fallback when optional persistence/OPFS APIs are unavailable; browser-row behavior, native quota limits, and large-file capability qualification remain open.

items.text: A fork/self-host deployment changes origin and configures its own supported Google/Microsoft public-client connector identity without changing canonical data schemas; where provider registration is unavailable, a qualified WebDAV/manual Vault path still permits zero-required-payment backup/portability without an Omnevum backend.

A mixed-language Vault is searched and summarized with the UI in a different locale; canonical source text remains unchanged, derived indexes/translations remain rebuildable/provenance-bound, and AI/tool actions use stable language-neutral semantic IDs.
items.notes: The current built preview retained English and French-authored text, switched the UI to fr-CA, searched an English token successfully, and retained locale/text after reload. Mixed-language Vault import/summary, AI/tool semantic-ID behavior, and target qualification remain open.

items.text: The user/owner requests a solution-shaped feature. The engineering system records or demonstrably applies XY analysis, finds a simpler existing/shared/FOSS/integration route that satisfies the underlying outcome, and avoids unnecessary new subsystem code without dropping material requested behavior.
items.notes: The Device/Input outcome was explicitly routed through the existing broker plus Acquire/Place owners after comparing ambient per-module APIs, a private device database, and a universal import subsystem. This proves one representative XY decision; broader owner-requested feature decisions and replacement-cost comparisons remain open.

items.text: The same large provider/export archive is imported twice. Acquire/Ingest recognizes source identity/content overlap, previews the reconciliation, avoids duplicate canonical records, preserves provenance, and reports any ambiguous conflicts instead of silently duplicating or overwriting user meaning.
items.notes: Deterministic idempotence/conflict tests and built Vault preview/merge evidence exist; large heterogeneous provider archives and full provenance/conflict UX remain open.

items.text: A heterogeneous personal-data export containing timeline events, artifacts, people, and locations is staged through Acquire/Ingest; raw/source identity remains inspectable, candidate mappings are previewable, and accepted records route to their canonical owners without creating a universal writable import database.
items.notes: Acquire now preserves one source digest/sequence and previews heterogeneous event, artifact, location, and person-shaped candidates while routing recognized rows to existing Time, Artifact, and Place owners without a universal import store; the current built preview staged and accepted all four synthetic rows with owner-labeled canonical output. Real provider exports, entity reconciliation, artifact payload retention, and target qualification remain open.

items.text: A document/photo/receipt is represented once by the Artifact capability and referenced from multiple authorized domain records; derived preview/OCR/index corruption can be rebuilt without duplicating or losing the canonical artifact/reference.
items.notes: Source/unit evidence proves one canonical Artifact payload can be referenced by two relationship records, survive derived search-index rebuild plus Vault payload round-trip, and now retain bounded PDF/image/HTML adapter metadata and DERIVED inert text where available. The current Chromium artifact accepts a 37-byte fixture through the visible file chooser, retains one platform.artifact record plus one payload, exposes the same record through shared selectors, and returns to a clean scoped origin. Real preview/OCR/thumbnail adapters, heavy-work cancellation under browser pressure, hostile rendering, and target qualification remain open.

items.text: A location/GPX/GeoJSON import is used by travel/timeline and another domain through shared Place/Geo semantics; disabling location tracking does not remove imported historical data or require continuous surveillance.
items.notes: The built preview captures a validated GeoJSON Point through the shared Place/Geo owner and preserves it as a canonical observation; the current artifact also stages and accepts a bounded GPX fixture through Acquire, routes a waypoint to platform.place and a track point to platform.time, and preserves coordinates/timestamp/source identity. Multi-track timeline composition, location-tracking policy, and broader import/target qualification remain open.

items.text: A user shares an explicitly bounded snapshot/projection. Linked private records, credentials, AI authority, attachments outside scope, and unrelated provenance do not transitively leak.
items.notes: The bounded projection owner scrubs credentials, unrelated links, private records, and provenance by default; the current built preview exercises active-grant authorization, explicit private-inclusion disclosure, and bounded export. Remote delivery, attachments, and cross-target qualification remain open.

items.text: A material upstream FOSS dependency publishes a new major release. Automation detects it, records release notes/currentness, stages an isolated candidate, runs characterization/contract/migration/target gates, and either adopts/adapts/defers/rejects it without modifying the accepted runtime until promotion.

A new FOSS entrant appears that provides a currently missing or locally bespoke capability with materially lower lifecycle cost. The ecosystem radar adds it to the Capability Coverage Matrix, performs exact source/license/security/fit evaluation, and either replaces/consolidates the old path after proof or records why not.

A high-severity vulnerability affects a shipped optional dependency. The security fast lane identifies affected scope, prevents false PASS, qualifies a fix/replacement or safely disables/degrades only the affected capability, and preserves unrelated core operation and user data.

An adopted FOSS component is removed from public package/repository infrastructure. The accepted Omnevum release continues to run, and the documented reconstruction path either succeeds from retained lawful inputs or reports the exact bounded reconstruction limitation without silently substituting content.

A copyleft FOSS capability is selected because it materially dominates alternatives. The release proves exact license/provenance/notice/corresponding-source obligations or isolates the component through a compliant integration; no license is silently misrepresented.

An upstream project adds functionality that supersedes an Omnevum local patch or duplicate subsystem. The maintenance cycle proves parity, removes the obsolete local path, reduces the patch/delta burden, and reruns affected regression/release evidence.

Before the initial shell/substrate architecture is frozen, the engineering system characterizes a current whole-app FOSS launchpad candidate such as NeumanOS and compares adapt/harvest/greenfield routes against static-host, mobile, local-first, accessibility, test, license, migration, and lifecycle criteria. The selected route records evidence that it is not an avoidable greenfield reinvention.
items.notes: NeumanOS and Kurumi are characterized at exact recorded identities and the small Omnevum foundation is selected as the Phase 0 launchpad; a fresh benchmark and full currentness/support/license/security comparison remain open.

items.text: The user creates one generic Track/Observe definition, records observations quickly from mobile, reuses the same canonical definition in multiple views/lenses, charts it through Visualize, and later maps selected observations into a specialist domain without duplicating or silently reclassifying source records.
items.notes: The historical built preview covers Track capture and derived dashboard rendering; the superseded artifact saved two observations through one reusable definition path and kept them as platform.track records. Mobile/touch qualification, multi-view permission breadth, and specialist-domain mapping remain open.

items.text: A large Vault uses qualified incremental repository mode to create two coherent snapshots with deduplication/chunk reuse, interrupt/resume an upload, verify integrity, prune unreachable data safely, and restore the selected snapshot through a different qualified transport without changing canonical IDs. The same product also supports a simple portable archive for a small Vault.

Omnevum preserves an external Web/document source as an Artifact with provenance plus a bounded standard/portable snapshot where allowed; derived extraction/thumbnail/index data can be rebuilt while user highlights/annotations remain separate canonical meaning linked to the source.
items.notes: Artifact provenance and separate source-linked annotation records are exercised locally, including active-anchor status; bounded inert HTML extraction now exists without active-content execution. External Web/document preservation, standard/portable snapshot policy, derived extraction/thumbnail rebuild, and target qualification remain open.

items.text: The game factory implements a nontrivial browser game using a qualified FOSS engine behind an Omnevum adapter, then upgrades or substitutes the engine in an isolated candidate while preserving Omnevum package/save/lifecycle contracts and rerunning game/browser/mobile/recovery evidence.
items.notes: The deterministic GameSession/package contract plus the factory benchmark and current Edge receipt prove a bounded nontrivial Constellation state machine with semantic input, pause/resume, responsive layout, save/load, accessible controls, and undeclared-action rejection. A qualified FOSS engine adapter, isolated candidate upgrade, Recovery integration, mobile/touch hardware, and broader target evidence remain open.

items.text: A material upstream-backed capability is tested against both the currently accepted upstream version and a candidate update using the same Omnevum-owned compatibility harness. A changed upstream behavior is detected before promotion; either the adapter/migration is updated and all affected evidence passes, or the candidate is rejected/deferred without ordinary domain modules silently inheriting the break.

A material canonical record is edited through several revisions; the user can inspect meaningful history/diff and safely revert an allowed change without using disaster backup. The owning domain's retention/deletion policy governs whether superseded sensitive revisions remain, and History/Version does not create a second writable copy or silently resurrect a deleted record.
items.notes: Local history/diff and command-path undo are covered; a superseded Chromium artifact exposed a visible Revert to revision action that created a new canonical revision and restored the prior task state. Domain retention policy, richer multi-revision UX, and target qualification remain open.

items.text: A user or qualified AI creates a declarative Compose/View definition containing a form, table/list, chart, and configurable dashboard arrangement over authorized canonical data. The view works on compact touch and expanded layouts, inherits theme/localization/accessibility, survives an Omnevum update, and every mutation still passes the owning semantic command/validation/permission path.
items.notes: Built-preview evidence covers declarative form/list/table/chart projection, localization, and semantic command boundaries; the current artifact also saves a safe-field dashboard over Track and Place records and proves canonical counts remain bounded. Configurable layout breadth, compact/expanded accessibility qualification, update survival, and qualified AI creation remain open.

items.text: A package uses a declarative automation predicate/rule. Malicious or malformed rule input cannot execute arbitrary JavaScript, access credentials/network/storage directly, or bypass confirmation/permission; a true rule only proposes an already-admitted semantic action.
items.notes: Source/unit evidence proves bounded data-only evaluation, prototype-path rejection, resource budgets, explicit admitted semantic-command IDs, and proposal-only output. A package-facing editor, execution adapter, permission/confirmation integration, and broader package qualification remain open.

items.text: Artifact/Acquire processes representative PDF, CSV, image metadata, and OCR-capable inputs through qualified browser-native adapters. Large/heavy work is cancellable/resource-bounded, original source identity/provenance is preserved, derived output is marked DERIVED, and hostile extracted/HTML content cannot execute active behavior.
items.notes: Source/unit evidence now proves bounded PDF metadata/action rejection, PNG dimensions without pixel decoding, inert HTML extraction with DERIVED text, explicit OCR NOT_CONFIGURED state, cancellation before inspection, source digest/provenance, payload retention, and idempotent PDF Acquire acceptance. Qualified browser-native OCR, PDF text/layout extraction, image OCR/thumbnail generation, large-file streaming, full cancellation/resource qualification, broader hostile-content and target evidence remain open.

items.text: The same logical Vault/replica identity can move between a vendor file transport and a qualified open personal-data/storage endpoint without changing canonical record IDs. Provider/schema-specific identifiers remain adapter metadata, and losing the remote endpoint does not prevent local core use.

Before Omnevum ships a bespoke general-purpose Vault/sync engine, the engineering system qualifies at least one close browser-native FOSS substrate such as SelfStore plus one materially different alternative such as remoteStorage/Etebase/Solid-compatible tooling. If a candidate satisfies the contract at lower lifecycle cost, it is adopted or adapter-wrapped; if not, the rejected capability gaps become tests for the selected implementation.
items.notes: SelfStore and remoteStorage.js are compared and dispositioned as isolated Phase 2 candidates; contract, security, quota, crash, migration, provider, and cross-origin qualification is not yet run.

items.text: A fresh AI engineer defines an ordinary record-oriented first-party package using package/domain schema plus Omnevum capability declarations and obtains a generated baseline list/detail/form/capture experience with responsive, accessible, localized, themed behavior. The generated UI contains no direct-store or permission bypass and can be replaced by a specialized hand-composed workflow without data migration.
items.notes: The package and record-app factory validate declarative manifests, canonical ownership, declared fields, command-owned capture/update/complete/archive, localized labels, Vault round-trip, and a generated baseline form/list view. The current Edge receipt now proves an actual generated browser capture/list surface with labelled controls and canonical persistence; fresh-agent creation, responsive matrix breadth, theme/mobile qualification, detail editing, and migration replacement evidence remain open.

items.text: A NeumanOS-class launchpad harvest assessment maps substantial working features to RETAIN, ADAPT, GENERALIZE, REPLACE, EXTERNALIZE, or DROP, identifies duplicate/local databases and high-authority seams, and proves that the selected fork/harvest/greenfield route preserves more qualified working value per lifecycle cost than the rejected routes.
items.notes: The harvest assessment records RETAIN/ADAPT/GENERALIZE/REPLACE-style boundaries and avoids importing a second application authority; quantitative lifecycle benchmarking and target/security qualification remain open.

items.text: The same canonical record participates in two user-defined Spaces/Scopes (for example Personal and Household or Work) without writable duplication. Search/Home/Assistant can be bounded to one Space, sharing one Space does not disclose out-of-scope linked records, and deleting the Space does not silently delete the underlying canonical record.
items.notes: The current artifact creates a user-defined Trip 2026 Space, exposes it in membership/filter/Compose/share selectors, assigns one canonical record through a platform.space overlay, and bounds Search to one result without duplication. Source/unit regression proves removal archives only the Space definition and deactivates memberships while retaining the underlying canonical record. Multi-user permission/share disclosure, Home/Assistant scoping, and broader target qualification remain open.

items.text: A representative large CSV/JSON/Parquet analytical dataset is queried locally through a qualified browser analytical projection engine such as DuckDB-Wasm without changing canonical ownership. The workload remains usable on the claimed target, cancellation/resource bounds work, required runtime assets are available under the static/offline profile, and remote extension/data fetch is not silently triggered.

Search is exercised against a representative multilingual/mobile Vault using at least two materially different qualified browser search candidates before the engine is frozen. The selected implementation proves rebuildability, permission-sensitive invalidation, acceptable mobile memory/latency, typo/prefix/ranking behavior required by the profile, and full-text operation without mandatory AI/vector embeddings.
items.notes: MiniSearch, FlexSearch, and Orama were compared on a multilingual 2,000-record fixture, and the selected owner now has a repeatable 10,000-record host guardrail (observed p95 57.39 ms, diagnostic heap delta 35,917,120 bytes). Mobile/browser memory-latency, ranking breadth, permission invalidation, and target qualification remain open.

items.text: A source permission or Space/Scope access change invalidates or filters affected full-text/vector/analytical derived projections so stale indexes, embeddings, query caches, or analytical tables cannot continue exposing data that the current authorized projection no longer includes.
items.notes: Scoped text search now applies authorized canonical IDs before derived-index tokenization, the UI computes Space scope before searching, and exact metadata-only BroadcastChannel events refresh external canonical views without carrying record content. Current local Chromium two-tab receipts cover canonical capture, user-defined Space creation, membership projection, whole-Space revocation with stale-scope reset, and individual membership revocation with zero scoped results while retaining the Space and source ownership; multi-user permission revocation, vector/analytical cache invalidation, external routes, and target qualification remain open.

items.text: Omnevum connects to a controlled browser-compatible MCP/standard tool endpoint through the AI/tool broker. An allowed tool can propose an admitted semantic action, while a malicious or changed tool schema/prompt cannot widen Vault context, obtain credentials, bypass Space/Scope or domain permissions, or directly mutate canonical state. Disconnecting or making the endpoint unavailable degrades only the optional integration and does not break the non-AI/core product.
items.notes: The optional ToolBroker validates endpoint descriptors against the admitted semantic-command set, projects explicit scrubbed context through ContextBroker, validates proposal output through the shared AI boundary, and returns an unavailable/degraded result on endpoint loss. A real browser-compatible MCP/standard endpoint, permission UI, provider/process isolation, and built-target qualification remain open.

items.text: The user highlights/comments on text and marks an image/PDF region using Annotate/Markup. The annotation remains a separate source-linked record with stable identity and provenance; exporting through a qualified portable annotation mapping preserves the relationship, while source modification that invalidates the anchor produces an explicit stale/orphan/ambiguous state rather than silently moving the annotation.
items.notes: Current built-artifact evidence proves quote-validated text annotation as a separate platform.annotate record with one active source anchor and no stale/orphaned anchors. Image/PDF regions, portable annotation export mapping, source-change invalidation states, and broader target qualification remain open.

items.text: A messy imported dataset is cleaned with previewed transformations, clustering/deduplication, and source/entity reconciliation. The accepted recipe/history is replayable/inspectable, ambiguous matches remain unresolved for review, and the original source plus provenance remain available; no fuzzy rule silently merges distinct canonical people/accounts/assets/records.

On a supported installed/browser target, the user shares text, a URL, or a supported file to Omnevum through the platform share sheet and reaches staged Capture/Acquire without bypassing validation/provenance. On a target without qualified share-target support, equivalent capture remains available through ordinary in-app URL/text/file/clipboard flows.
items.notes: Local Chromium static-preview evidence covers ordinary in-app file and clipboard fallback flows plus the current manifest GET query handoff through staged Acquire and canonical acceptance with IMPORT provenance. Real platform share-sheet delivery, supported-browser qualification, installed-target behavior, and file-share payloads remain open.

items.text: The user imports bibliographic data from at least two qualified interchange families such as BibTeX/RIS/CSL-JSON, links a reference to an Artifact/source plus user annotations, and renders citations/bibliography through a selectable style. Changing the style changes only derived presentation; it does not mutate source/evidence identity or annotation truth.

A spatial Compose/View canvas contains freeform drawing plus references to canonical records. Moving/styling/grouping referenced nodes changes only view state unless the user invokes an admitted semantic command; a standalone drawing can be exported/backed up as an Artifact, and upgrading/replacing the underlying canvas engine does not require canonical-record migration.

The user captures an ambiguous mixed item into the universal inbox. Triage/Clarify preserves the raw source and provenance, proposes possible owner/type/actions without silently committing them, lets the user split/link/route/defer/reference/delete through admitted commands, and closes the staging item without leaving duplicate writable copies. A separate unambiguous capture can bypass the inbox through an explicit safe route.
items.notes: Explicit review, defer, clarify, reference, archive, idempotent link, bounded Note/Task route, split, safe-direct, and delete actions use the revision-checked canonical CommandBus path; compound transitions commit atomically, and the built inbox now shows deterministic proposal-only owner/type/action guidance without canonical mutation. AI/richer proposal breadth, native fault-injection, broader accessibility/target qualification, and complete triage UX remain open.

items.text: The user performs a representative local document-finishing workflow such as annotate/fill/sign/mark, redact, page reorder, merge/split, compress, or convert using qualified browser-native FOSS. Omnevum preserves the original source by default, emits a derived Artifact with provenance, works without uploading the content, and does not misrepresent a visual signature/mark as a separately qualified legal/cryptographic signature.
items.notes: A bounded local text/inert-HTML redaction path is implemented behind Artifact ownership and is exercised on the current local Chromium artifact with a synthetic hostile HTML fixture. It preserves the source, strips active HTML, emits a lineage-linked DERIVED Artifact, and fails closed on unsupported, truncated, oversized, unmatched, and cancelled input. Normal OS file-picker/human interaction, qualified PDF/office/editor adapters, broader accessibility/target qualification, and FOSS/round-trip evidence remain open.

items.text: A user creates an external connector action while offline. Effect/Outbox persists one typed operation, the app/browser is restarted, and replay occurs only after current authority/credential/Space/destination revalidation. An injected ambiguous remote response enters OUTCOME_UNKNOWN/RECONCILE and is reconciled before retry; the final external system contains no duplicate effect, or any unavoidable duplication risk is surfaced truthfully.
items.notes: The platform runner plus the provider-neutral JsonEndpointEffectExecutor prove crash recovery through OUTCOME_UNKNOWN/RECONCILE, no-blind-replay behavior, persisted exponential backoff, maxAttempts terminal exhaustion, expiry, guard denial, bounded effect storage, idempotency headers, secret-free payloads, brokered authorization, bounded HTTP classification, and an IndexedDB status compare-and-set that prevents concurrent runners from executing one pending operation twice. The shipped app now lets a user stage one typed external action locally with persisted authority/permission/Space/disclosure/schema context, preserves it across reload without automatic network execution, routes explicit runs only to the exact persisted destination, revalidates the current context before executor use, and visibly promotes an ambiguous attempt to RECONCILE. The accessible app-owned confirmation dialog and CORS-capable loopback fixture are receipt-bound. Same-origin Edge/Chromium previews cover synthetic response-loss/reconciliation, a browser reload/process-restart run through the live loopback adapter with one creation and one reconciliation, and credentialed bearer delivery with one creation and no duplicate creation; the browser credentialed path keeps raw secret material in session memory only. The unit broker contract now proves host-mediated opaque-handle rehydration after process restart without secret persistence. Real provider/remote deployment, browser/host restart restoration, shipped connector OAuth/PKCE or ACL integration, and broader target evidence remain open.

items.text: A reminder becomes due while Omnevum is closed on a target without qualified exact background scheduling. Omnevum does not falsely claim it notified at the due time; on next open/resume it deterministically surfaces the missed/overdue reminder. On a separately qualified external-calendar or ntfy/Gotify-class companion profile, stronger delivery may occur without making that companion a core dependency.
items.notes: Fresh local Chromium tab-close/reopen evidence proves canonical persistence and truthful Due on resume surfacing; exact background scheduling, native process-close behavior, companion delivery, and broader target qualification remain open.

items.text: A user enables a supported passkey/WebAuthn device-unlock wrapper for protected Vault/recovery secret access, then loses that browser profile or migrates Omnevum to a different HTTPS origin. Portable recovery using the independent recovery secret/key still succeeds, the old origin-bound passkey is not falsely treated as portable ownership, and the user can re-enroll a new local wrapper after restore.

A connector/API credential is stored/used through the credential/key broker. Ordinary modules, declarative views/rules, diagnostics, ordinary Vault export, and model-visible AI context cannot read the raw reusable credential; revoking/locking it invalidates future broker effects and pending Effect/Outbox replay without deleting unrelated canonical data.
items.notes: The session-only broker exposes secret-free metadata, bounds secret callbacks, rejects raw credential fields in effect payloads, exposes the canonical EffectRunner authorization seam, and cancels a pending brokered operation after revocation before executor use. Its unit contract now proves that a fresh broker can rehydrate the same opaque handle only through a non-secret recovery reference and fresh secret material while retaining SESSION_MEMORY storage. The shipped Recovery ledger displays effect status, destination, retry budget, Space context, and action state without rendering payloads or credential handles; the new revalidation guard also delegates credential validity to the broker. The explicit run confirmation is now app-owned and accessible, but persisted connector integration, diagnostics/Vault/AI-context exclusion, browser-side post-revocation proof, and target qualification remain open.

items.text: An authorized set of canonical records is exported/projected through a qualified JSON-LD/RDF semantic-graph profile and queried/validated with a browser-local SPARQL/SHACL-class engine. Source IDs/provenance/disclosure boundaries are preserved, inferred/validation/query results remain DERIVED, and importing graph data routes through Acquire/Triage rather than directly mutating canonical owners.

Before the initial whole-app route is frozen, current NeumanOS and Kurumi candidates are both characterized when still materially relevant. The engineering decision records which working features/code/tests are retained/harvested/adapted/replaced, and demonstrates that the selected combined fork/harvest/greenfield route dominates the rejected routes on static-host fit, canonical ownership, mobile/accessibility, security, updateability, and time-to-accepted-result.
items.notes: Both launchpad candidates are characterized and the selected route preserves Omnevum ownership; a current comparative benchmark across all listed dimensions remains open before final route closure.

items.text: A user with an eligible paid AI subscription enables a provider-supported subscription route through the official SDK/agent/CLI or a qualified local companion without entering an API key. An Omnevum workflow uses only the authorized context projection, the result is marked DERIVED with route/provenance, and disabling the companion leaves all non-AI/core functions intact.

The selected subscription route reaches its included quota or reports uncertain quota state. Omnevum does not silently purchase credits, activate usage-based billing, switch to a metered API key, or widen disclosure. It stops/degrades or moves only to another route explicitly allowed by the user's route policy.

Provider currentness marks a consumer-web/OAuth-piggyback technique as TERMS_BLOCKED (for example current ChatGPT web automatic extraction or current Google legacy Gemini-CLI OAuth harvesting). Omnevum refuses that programmatic route without attempting stealth/browser impersonation and instead offers an official subscription agent, reverse integration, manual handoff, local model, or explicit API route where available.

A plan/workspace that supports a reverse app/MCP/connector integration lets an external subscribed assistant query a deliberately bounded Omnevum projection. Read-only provider limits remain read-only; a write-capable provider action still traverses Omnevum's semantic-command/permission/Effect-Outbox path. Removing the external integration revokes future access without deleting canonical records.

The engineering factory completes the same representative stateful work item under two materially different qualified agent hosts, with at least one current FOSS/open host when practical and at least one current subscription-backed official agent when the owner has that entitlement. The durable controller/evidence lets work resume after switching hosts without replaying owner decisions from chat.
items.notes: The current clean-checkout benchmark proves durable controller/evidence reconstruction and interruption/resume without original conversation state on one qualified host. A materially different second agent host, including the owner-entitled subscription-backed route where applicable, remains unqualified.

items.text: Camera/photo, microphone/audio, file/share/clipboard, geolocation, and barcode/QR capture are exercised through the Device/Input broker on supported profiles. Permission denial/cancellation releases resources and degrades to qualified manual/file alternatives; no module retains ambient camera/mic/location authority, and captured data routes through Artifact/Acquire/Track/Place/Triage rather than a private device database.
items.notes: Source/unit evidence plus current Edge and in-app-browser artifacts cover capability detection, an explicit user-triggered Device/Input surface, bounded file/clipboard input, manual fallback, browser-native QR detection when exposed, filtered bounded results, and automatic media-track release. The current receipts prove the visible routing/no-retention boundary without invoking permissions or transmitting data. Real camera/microphone/geolocation permission denial/cancellation, hardware capture routing through Artifact/Acquire/Track/Place/Triage, browser/device breadth, assistive technology, and human acceptance remain open.

items.text: Local AI is exercised against at least two materially different qualified browser runtimes or one runtime plus a browser-native built-in API where available. Model download/cache, WebGPU/WASM capability detection, worker/main-thread behavior, cancellation, memory/storage pressure, offline reuse and route fallback are measured before the runtime is frozen.

A representative rich document/spreadsheet/canvas workflow is satisfied by a qualified reusable editor/office component or external-office integration rather than bespoke engine code. The editor does not gain global storage/AI/permission/sync authority, is lazy-loaded where heavy, and import/export round-trip loss is tested/reported.

The first release containing adopted/copied FOSS runs an automated compliance pipeline that generates dependency/source/license inventory, notices/attribution and SBOM data, identifies applicable source/corresponding-source obligations, and fails closed on unresolved policy-critical findings instead of relying on a manually maintained notice list.
items.notes: The clean CI path now regenerates the dependency SBOM and a lockfile-bound attribution/source-obligation receipt, and the license audit fails closed on missing package metadata, stale receipts, incomplete attribution coverage, or policy-critical findings. Exact copyright/notice rights, corresponding-source fulfillment, and legal distribution review remain open.

items.text: If executable third-party extension support is claimed, a qualified isolation substrate passes adversarial tests for global/prototype escape, network/storage access, CPU/memory abuse, message validation, update revocation and capability leakage. If it does not, the release still supports declarative extensions but truthfully leaves executable third-party packages disabled.
items.notes: The accepted baseline admits declarative extensions and explicitly disables unqualified executable third-party packages. No executable isolation substrate is claimed; adversarial sandbox, update-revocation, and target qualification remain open if that profile changes.

items.text: A representative large personal-health/wearable export is ingested through USER_EXPORT_IMPORT on a static-browser target with streaming/resource bounds, provenance, idempotent re-import and explicit subject identity. On a target with no direct browser HealthKit/Health Connect access, Omnevum reports PLATFORM_LIMITED instead of pretending direct access; an optional native/local companion can be enabled and removed without changing canonical IDs or breaking the file-import path.

A person-specific sharing/delegation grant is created for a bounded purpose/Space/data set, used for an authorized projection/effect, then revoked. Future share/effect attempts are blocked after revalidation, stale derived/share state is reconciled as required, and neither household/contact membership nor provider ACLs silently recreate the grant.
items.notes: The current local workbench creates a purpose/Space/record-bound grant, enforces the declared Space including membership overlays, requires the grant for projection, disables export after canonical revocation, and persists the revoked state; external effect use, provider ACL interaction, stale share reconciliation, and target qualification remain open.

items.text: A provider whose current terms explicitly permit browser automation is exercised through a qualified user-controlled browser bridge and the same bounded AI Context Broker. The route does not scrape or reuse unrelated session data, bypass protective measures, exceed allowed automation scope, or become the sole AI path. Changing the provider's currentness state to TERMS_BLOCKED disables the route without data loss or hidden fallback.

A local terms-aware Subscription Bridge discovers at least two officially authenticated provider agent/CLI surfaces the user already pays for, exposes them through typed provider-specific adapters without exporting raw session credentials to the PWA, and routes a bounded task according to capability/cost/currentness policy. A provider route known to prohibit third-party OAuth/session piggybacking is absent or TERMS_BLOCKED even if a community bridge could technically invoke it; disabling the bridge leaves canonical data and non-AI core behavior intact.

If a release/profile admits downloadable offline maps, Place/Geo downloads a bounded offline map region through a qualified MapLibre/PMTiles-class route, reports expected size/quota and data attribution before or during acquisition as appropriate, remains usable without network, and can remove/reacquire the replaceable map package without changing canonical place/route identities. A target without the selected OPFS path degrades to an admitted fallback or PLATFORM_LIMITED state rather than losing canonical Place/Geo data.

If a camera-document-scanning workflow is admitted, the user scans a multipage document through Device/Input using a qualified browser-local scanner path. Raw captured page frames remain recoverable until the owning workflow deliberately discards them; crop/corners/rotation/filter/perspective changes are represented as reversible derived edit state through preview/export; heavy CV work does not block the camera UI; cancellation/permission denial releases resources; and the resulting PDF/image Artifact carries source/provenance without creating a scanner-owned document database.

If a release claims in-browser editing of DOCX/XLSX/PPTX-class artifacts, a representative workflow is exercised through a qualified static/browser-only office component with no required document server or content upload. Heavy editor assets are lazy/offline qualified, host-owned save/provenance remains under Artifact, exact round-trip limitations are reported, and applicable copyleft/trademark/notice obligations are satisfied in the candidate release.

If live browser-to-browser collaboration is admitted, two authorized browser clients establish a session through a qualified WebRTC/Trystero-class transport from the static-host product, and a separately qualified relay-free QR/libp2p path is exercised on a compatible network when that profile is claimed. Loss of signalling/relay availability, restrictive NAT, client isolation, or suspension degrades only the affected live path; possession of a room/link/QR payload or peer connection alone does not grant data authority; revocation blocks future admitted writes/disclosure; and durable canonical state/Recovery does not depend on an ephemeral peer session.

If local speech recognition or synthesis is admitted, the claimed local-speech profile is exercised through materially different qualified browser routes where practical, such as whisper.cpp WASM, sherpa-onnx WebAssembly, or Transformers.js/Kokoro-class TTS. Model/runtime downloads are explicit and reclaimable, unsupported SIMD/WebGPU/memory conditions degrade cleanly, microphone authority stays with Device/Input, retained transcripts/audio-derived meaning remain DERIVED until adopted, and no cloud speech route is silently activated.

If the accepted profile admits iCalendar/vCard recurrence import or standards-based calendar interchange, Time imports a representative iCalendar source containing recurrence, time-zone transitions and at least one ambiguous/nonexistent local-time edge. A qualified ICAL.js-class route or proven equivalent preserves the applicable source semantics; Temporal-dependent arithmetic is capability-detected with a qualified fallback where required; recurrence expansion is resource-bounded; and export/re-import does not silently shift canonical instants, wall times, time zones or recurrence meaning.

If browser-local media editing/conversion is admitted, a representative large media Artifact is probed, trimmed or transformed through a qualified Mediabunny/WebCodecs-class route when supported, with streaming/cancellation/resource bounds and original-source preservation. Unsupported codecs or target APIs degrade to a separately qualified fallback such as FFmpeg-Wasm or explicit PLATFORM_LIMITED state; no upload or transcoding route is silently widened.

If a release/profile renders untrusted HTML/markup, a hostile fixture set including mutation-XSS/DOM-clobbering style cases is processed by the admitted rendering path. Native Sanitizer API use occurs only on support rows where qualified; a maintained DOMPurify-class fallback or equivalent blocks active behavior on other claimed rows; sanitizer bypass/currentness changes invalidate affected evidence; and sanitized presentation still grants no network, credential, canonical-write or external-effect authority.

If WARC/WACZ preservation or replay is admitted, a representative archive is parsed through a qualified browser streaming implementation and replayed through a qualified Webrecorder-class path without installing an independent same-origin service worker. Archived active content cannot regain ambient live-network, credential, canonical-write or external-effect authority, and disabling/removing replay leaves the source Artifact and annotations intact.

If an official release profile claims cryptographic signing or supply-chain attestation, the exact release artifact digest is verified against its signed bundle/attestation through a qualified open scheme such as Sigstore/cosign or in-toto-compatible metadata. Verification remains possible using the retained verification material required by the claim; provenance is not presented as safety assurance; and any identity/transparency-log disclosure is explicit in the release profile rather than a hidden side effect.

If Place/Geo admits nontrivial client-side spatial analysis, representative GeoJSON operations such as distance, intersection/buffer or simplification are exercised through a qualified modular engine such as Turf before bespoke geometry is accepted. Results remain DERIVED, coordinate/reference assumptions are explicit, pathological inputs are resource-bounded, and upgrading/replacing the geometry engine does not change canonical place identities.

If spreadsheet import/export is admitted, representative XLSX/ODS/CSV-class fixtures are processed through a qualified browser-capable FOSS route such as SheetJS Community Edition where fit. Source/release identity follows the canonical upstream, active content/macros remain inert, formula/value/type/date-loss behavior is reported and tested, and import/export does not turn a spreadsheet parser into canonical domain ownership.
